messages.subject: Connecting RApache to a database?
messages.body_plain:
Hi there,

I'm pretty new to R and RApache (only started using it last week!) but I have been tasked with a project which requires me to retrieve information from a database and then display this on a web page using graphs.

I have successfully set up RApache and I have managed to get a few of the simple examples (rnorm graphs) working so my next aim is to set up a test DB and see if I can use a select statement to simply print out the data. The problem I'm having is I don't really know how to connect to a DB using RApache? I have had a look online and found 'REvalOnStartup' but again I don't really know how this works or even where I would configure it?

Thanks in advance!

messages.subject: Re: Connecting RApache to a database?
messages.body_plain:
RApache is just responsible for exposing R functions for the web. As far as I concern, you should look for how to use R to connect to a DB, and then set RApache to run this code on startup, making the connection available to calls.
—

messages.subject: Re: RApache while loop
messages.body_plain:
Hi, Don:

The first thing to do is verify that your code works in an interactive R session.  If it doesn't work in an interactive R session, I would recommend posting to the R topic on stackexchange.com <http://stackexchange.com>, where you can get general programming help.  If it does, then you should try writing the results of your code to stderr, so it ends up in the Apache log.  Something like this (untested):

  data <- tryCatch({
    rs <- dbSendQuery(con, paste("select * from test"))
    fetch(rs)
  },
  error=function(e) e)
  if (inherits(data, "error")) {
    cat(data, "\n", file=stderr())
  } else {
    # Format and return to the browser.
  }

Regards,

Nick

messages.subject: Re: RApache while loop
messages.body_plain:
Hi, Dom:

What I meant by interactive R session is just that R is usually used ... interactively.  Some people use an IDE [1]; others just run R from a terminal.  In both cases, though, the effect is the same: you type R code at a prompt, and the code is executed when you complete a statement (i.e. enter a complete line of code and press return.)  If you're just learning R, learning how to write the language in one of these interactive environments will take you a long way towards being able to know how to plot data.

Regards,

Nick

[1] For example, http://www.rstudio.com/products/rstudio/download/
